subject: Imprecise Dirichlet in Stan (for Bayesian rank-sum & signed-rank instead of Wilcoxon/Friedman)

messages.author: 7f3dcb786c576e61
messages.subject: Imprecise Dirichlet in Stan (for Bayesian rank-sum & signed-rank instead of Wilcoxon/Friedman)
parts:
Dear Stan list/users,

Has anyone implemented something similar to the so called Imprecise Dirichlet Process in Stan? 
The authors of a set of papers describing the use of this "IDP" describes it like this on the home page:
"IDP is based on a Prior Near-Ignorance Dirichlet Process. This is the class of all Dirichlet Processes obtained by fixing the prior strength of the Dirichlet Process and letting the normalized base measure vary in the set of all probability measures."
http://ipg.idsia.ch/software/IDP.php

and they provide R (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/IDPSurvival/index.html) and Matlab source code. However it seems the license is GPL so I'd rather have Stan implementations that are fully free and not look at their code.

From their related papers I found this which seems to describe the general idea ( http://arxiv.org/pdf/1402.2755v2.pdf ):

"...the use of an almost vacuous model which they
call “near-ignorance” or “imprecise” model. This is a model that behaves a priori as a vacuous
model for some basic inferences (e.g., prior mean, prior credible regions) but it always provides
non-vacuous posterior inferences"

and then:

"The main aim of this
paper is to derive a prior near-ignorance DP, called Imprecise DP (IDP). This is the class T of all
DPs obtained by fixing the prior strength of the DP and letting the normalized base measure vary
in the set of all probability measures. We will show that the IDP behaves a priori as a vacuous
model for all predictive inferences. This, together with the fact that it is a nonparametric model,
allows us to start a statistical analysis with very weak assumptions about the problem of interest.
However, contrarily to a full vacuous model, we will show that the IDP can learn from data"

Has anyone seen this or related models implemented in Stan or is there something hindering their implementation?

Any pointers or advice appreciated.

Thanks,

Robert Feldt

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Imprecise Dirichlet in Stan (for Bayesian rank-sum & signed-rank instead of Wilcoxon/Friedman)
parts:
Stan requires a fixed parameter set, so the bestyou can
do is approximate a DP with a large-K Dirichlet.

We recommend completely the opposite approach to
priors, which incorporate as much information you have.
There's a wiki page on prior recommendations and also
a long discussion in the manual.

And be careful. Many purportedly "vague" and "noninformative"
priors usually don't behave the way people expect them to in practice.
For instance, in an LDA model, the scale of the prior has
an enormous impact on the topics found and how many topics
are assigned per document. Because it's a Dirichlet, the
uniform distribution is Dirichlet(1). Then when you go
Dirichlet(epsilon) for epsilon << 1, the prior's focusing
increasing weight on there being a sparse solution.

And just a heads up: RStan and PyStan are under GPL.
It's only the math library, core Stan library, and CmdStan
that are BSD licensed.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Imprecise Dirichlet in Stan (for Bayesian rank-sum & signed-rank instead of Wilcoxon/Friedman)
parts:
> On Jun 17, 2016, at 3:42 AM, Robert Feldt <robert...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Thanks Bob, I appreciate this. Very useful.
>
> I will try to stay with informative priors then but to me it is less clear to see how to set them for a Dirichlet than for some other distributions.

Just think of the Dirichlet as the multinomial generalization
of the beta and the same tehcniques apply:

parameters {
real<lower=0> kappa; // prior count + K
simplex[K] theta; // prior mean
...
transformed parameters {
real<lower=0> alpha;
alpha <- kappa * theta;
...
model {
theta ~ dirichlet(alpha);
...

Still, the Dirichlet is not very expressive as it only specifies
a mean and overall concentration, not covariance.
> I have found the discussions about priors in the Stan manual but not sure I know which wiki page you refer to, do you have a link?
